summary: Augusta County, VA summit tower from the 1920s to 1975, removed after vandalism; foundations photographed June 2009; summit now a viewpoint on a paved road.

facts.status_note: Removed in 1975 after vandalism per the register; foundations photographed June 2009; no later description of the site found

staffing.status: Forest Service towermen on duty in 1937; no later staffing found in the sources read

access.note: Summit reached by a one-lane paved road ending at a paved parking lot (Friends of Shenandoah Mountain); Wikipedia says a narrow paved road reaches the summit from Harrisonburg; road often iced in winter. Forest Service listing not checked.

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The paved road ends at a parking lot on the summit, which the Friends describe as a viewpoint; the road is often icy in winter and early spring.

events.note: Forest Service towermen on duty at the Reddish Knob tower; 138 visitors registered at the lookout cabin over one weekend (Harrisonburg Daily News Record item)
Two-way radio and portable field telephone stolen from the lookout tower; located (Daily News Record item dated October 14, 1960)
Tower removed after persistent problems with vandalism (register); Forest Lookouts also gives 1975
Registered June 23, 2009; nominated by Brian M. Powell; foundations pictured in June 2009

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The brief said Reddish Knob shares a register number with another record. Reddish Knob is FFLOS US 523, VA 1. The Forest Lookouts Virginia list shows High Knob (GWNF) as NHLR US 76, VA 1. Only the state number VA 1 matches; the US numbers differ, so these are two separate records.

notes_for_editor: The brief's source list includes the Friends of Shenandoah Mountain History of High Knob Fire Tower page; that page is about a different tower, so it is not cited here. A Friends article 'What Ever Happened to Reddish Knob Tower?' is linked from the FFLOS listing. Search snippets describe a 1972 Forest Service proposal that would have removed all towers except Elliott Knob and Reddish Knob, and a $400 dismantling by local men. The page text was not retrieved, so neither claim is in the story; it should be fetched and checked, since the 1972 exemption would conflict with the 1975 removal. Build date: the sources give only 'the 1920s'. Access is public per the Friends page and Wikipedia; the Forest Service listing was not checked. No source describes the foundations today.
